definition: A decoding strategy (also called nucleus sampling) that samples from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds a threshold p.
details: Unlike top-k, top-p dynamically adjusts how many tokens are considered based on the shape of the probability distribution, often producing more natural and varied text.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. Here is the short version: A decoding strategy (also called nucleus sampling) that samples from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds a threshold p. The part that makes it sing: Unlike top-k, top-p dynamically adjusts how many tokens are considered based on the shape of the probability distribution, often producing more natural and varied text. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. And that is Top-p Sampling — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.

citation.title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
